//: Typecheck config for the serverless functions.
WHY IT LIVES IN api/ RATHER THAN AS tsconfig.api.json AT THE ROOT:
Vercel's Node builder type-checks each function against the NEAREST
tsconfig.json. With this file absent it walked up to the root config —
which is the browser one: DOM lib, vite/client types, include: ['src'] —
and reported 'Cannot find name process' on every function that reads an
environment variable. The build survived it, but the checking was
meaningless, which is the same as not having it.
WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM THE ROOT CONFIG AT ALL: the root config is built
for the browser. api/ runs on Node as ESM, so it needs Node types and no
DOM. Folding them together would either weaken the browser config or fail
Run locally via `pnpm typecheck`, which checks both this and the root.
ON `lib: [ES2022, DOM]`: DOM is here for fetch/Response/Headers, not for
the browser. Node has had a global fetch since 18 and these functions use
it to call the CRM, but the type declarations for it live in the DOM lib.
Without it, Vercel's function typecheck reports 'Property json does not
exist on type Response' on every CRM call. Nothing in api/ touches window
or document; the root config remains the one that owns browser settings.
